title: accessor.Context is null when using DataLoader with a custom document executor
body:
## Summary

In my Startup file I have the following configuration:
```cs
        public class CustomDocumentExecuter : DocumentExecuter { }

        public void ConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services)
        {
            GraphQL.MicrosoftDI.GraphQLBuilderExtensions
                .AddGraphQL(services)
                .AddServer(true)
                .AddSystemTextJson()
                .AddErrorInfoProvider(opt => opt.ExposeExceptionStackTrace = Environment.IsDevelopment())
                .AddDocumentExecuter<CustomDocumentExecuter>()
                .AddSchema<StarWarsSchema>()
                .AddGraphTypes(typeof(StarWarsSchema).Assembly)
                .AddDataLoader();
        }
```

The StarWarsSchema contains a field that uses the DataLoader in the usual way:
```
            Field<StringGraphType>(
                "batchedName",
                resolve: context => accessor.Context.GetOrAddBatchLoader<string, string>(
                    "LoadName", data.NameById).LoadAsync(context.Source.Id)
                );
```

Everything works as expected if I leave out the `AddDocumentExecuter` call in the configuration, or if I add the standard `DocumentExecuter`. However, when I add the `CustomDocumentExecuter` above, even though it does not override anything, the dataloader accessor does not work any more - the `accessor.Context` then always gives `null`. The rest seems to work, only the fields using DataLoader show the problem.

Am I doing anything wrong or is this a bug? How can I use a custom DocumentExecuter together with the DataLoader?

### Environment

```
    <TargetFramework>net6.0</TargetFramework>
```
```
    <PackageReference Include="GraphQL" Version="4.7.1" />
    <PackageReference Include="GraphQL.DataLoader" Version="4.7.1" />
    <PackageReference Include="GraphQL.MicrosoftDI" Version="4.7.1" />
    <PackageReference Include="GraphQL.Server.Core" Version="5.2.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="GraphQL.Server.Transports.AspNetCore" Version="5.2.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="GraphQL.Server.Transports.AspNetCore.SystemTextJson" Version="5.2.0" />
```
author: Cito

comments.body: Just guessing but your custom document executor probably doesn’t have the proper constructor that allows dependency injection to inject all the necessary classes. You need the most complex one available for proper operation.
No, that is the recommended pattern.
Thanks a lot, @Shane32, you saved my day.

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of why the DataLoader doesn't work with a custom DocumentExecuter
Guidance on properly implementing a custom DocumentExecuter that works with DataLoader
Confirmation that their approach to changing execution strategy is appropriate

_classification.category: Can be dockerized without any issue

title: Classes derived from InputObjectGraphType *sometimes* return error when given a name and a field is given a description.
author: bigbizze

comments.body: Name is a GraphType's name, not description. Name must have only alphanumeric symbols. Try the latest preview version and you will see runtime error about that when schema is built.
Ah, this makes sense then why it would often confuse one input type for another. Good to know, not sure how I mixed up the name and description properties so thoroughly, thank you!

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of the correct usage of the Name property in GraphType classes
Clarification on why the error occurs with certain naming patterns
Information about the distinction between name and description properties in GraphQL types

_classification.category: Can be dockerized without any issue
